official_statement_rationale: With headline CPI inflation at 7.44 per cent, we are in the midst of a significant breach of the upper tolerance limit. The surge in food inflation to 11.51 per cent, compounded by a 5 per cent monsoon deficit, poses a clear and present danger of unanchoring inflation expectations. While I acknowledge the resilience of GVA growth at 7.80 per cent and the moderation in core inflation to 4.90 per cent, history warns us that supply-side shocks can rapidly permeate into generalized inflation if the monetary policy response is not sufficiently firm. A positive output gap of 0.60 per cent indicates that the economy is operating above its potential, providing space for further tightening. Given the persistence of these shocks, I believe a 25 basis point increase is necessary to demonstrate our unwavering commitment to the 4 per cent target and to prevent the current inflation trajectory from becoming entrenched. However, in deference to the collective wisdom of the Committee, I shall align with the majority on the repo rate while maintaining my firm stance on the withdrawal of accommodation.
